definition_zh: 便士；一便士硬币；美分；（否定）一分钱
definition_en: a small British coin worth one hundredth of a pound, its value as a unit of money, or an American one-cent coin
core_image: 一枚磨得发亮的铜色小圆片躺在掌心
scene: 集市收摊时，摊主把零散的硬币一枚枚数进铁盒。She counted the pennies into a small tin box.
sceneCN: 这里是「一便士硬币」（第 2 个义项：一枚枚具体的硬币）；句意为她把一便士硬币数进小铁盒。

senses.title: A unit of British money
senses.definition: a unit of money in Britain, worth one hundredth of a pound, used mainly when stating prices and amounts
senses.definitionCN: 英国的货币单位，等于一英镑的百分之一，主要用于说明价格和金额
senses.example: The stamp costs fifty pence.
senses.exampleCN: 这张邮票要五十便士。
senses.why: When the coin is treated as a value on a price tag, English uses pence, the old plural that behaves like a unit rather than a set of objects.
senses.whyCN: 当这枚钱被当成价签上的数值时，英语用 pence；这个旧复数更像一个计量单位，而不是一堆具体物件。

senses.title: A single British coin
senses.definition: the small coin itself, especially when you count or hold separate pieces
senses.definitionCN: 指那枚小硬币本身，尤指数着一枚枚、拿在手里的零散硬币
senses.example: He dropped two pennies into the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 他把两枚一便士硬币投进罐子。
senses.why: The regular plural pennies is kept for the physical pieces, so English can tell the object in your palm from the figure on a receipt.
senses.whyCN: 规则复数 pennies 留给一枚枚实物，因此英语能区分手心那枚东西和收据上的那个数字。

senses.title: An American one-cent coin
senses.definition: in American informal use, a coin worth one cent, or one cent itself
senses.definitionCN: 在美式口语中，指值一分的硬币，或指一分钱
senses.example: The machine only takes pennies and nickels.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只收一分和五分硬币。
senses.why: American speech kept the old Germanic name for small change instead of the Latin cent, so penny crossed the Atlantic with a new value.
senses.whyCN: 美国口语保留了表示零钱的古老日耳曼名称，而没有用拉丁来源的 cent，于是 penny 漂过大西洋后换了面值。

senses.title: The smallest amount of money
senses.definition: used after a negative to mean no money at all, or an amount too small to matter
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定词之后，表示一分钱也没有，或指少到无关紧要的钱
senses.example: It did not cost me a penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这没花我一分钱。
senses.why: Since a penny is the smallest unit, denying even one of them denies everything, and that is how the word became a way of saying total lack.
senses.whyCN: 一便士是最小单位，连一枚都否认就等于否认全部，这个词便由此成了「完全没有」的说法。

intro.en: Penny is an old Germanic word for a small coin; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: penny 是日耳曼语中表示小硬币的古老词，更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed form for a small coin; the exact meaning and origin of the stem are uncertain.
items.cn: 这是重构出来的「小硬币」形式；词干的确切含义与来源都不确定。

items.en: Old English had penig and pening for a penny, a coin and a unit of account.
items.cn: 古英语写作 penig 或 pening，既指硬币，也指记账单位。

items.en: Middle English simplified the spelling to peni and used penies as the regular plural.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写简化为 peni，并用 penies 作规则复数。

items.en: Speakers split the plural in two: pence for an amount of money, pennies for separate coins.
items.cn: 使用者把复数一分为二：pence 指金额，pennies 指一枚枚硬币。

items.en: Decimal coinage from 1971 kept the penny, and American English uses the same word for its one-cent coin.
items.cn: 一九七一年起的十进制币制保留了 penny，美式英语也用同一个词指一分硬币。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the plural forms, derived words and compounds of the coin name; the near-meaning group collects other small units of money.
note.cn: 形近组收这枚硬币名称的复数形式、派生词与复合词；近义组收其他小额货币单位。

entries.definition: The plural used when a penny is counted as an amount of money.
entries.definitionCN: 把便士当作金额计算时使用的复数。

entries.definition: Having no money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 身无分文的。

entries.definition: A former British coin worth six old pennies.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧时值六便士的硬币。

entries.definition: A former British coin worth half a penny.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧时值半便士的硬币。

entries.definition: A unit of money worth one hundredth of a dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一美元百分之一的货币单位。

entries.definition: A piece of metal money.
entries.definitionCN: 金属制成的钱币。

entries.definition: Coins of low value returned or kept after paying.
entries.definitionCN: 付款后找回或留下的零钱。

entries.definition: British informal for a coin of low value.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语，指低面值的铜币。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old coin name with two plurals, and its family grows through English compounds and suffixes rather than Latin parts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古老的硬币名，带着两个复数；同族词靠英语的复合与后缀生长，而不是拉丁部件。

normal.en: Old English penig is the direct ancestor, and the spelling changed but the small coin stayed.
normal.cn: 古英语 penig 是直系祖先，拼写变了，小硬币的意思没变。

normal.en: Pence answers how much, pennies answers how many pieces, which is why a price list never says pennies.
normal.cn: pence 回答「多少钱」，pennies 回答「几枚」，所以价目表从不写 pennies。

normal.en: The suffix -less in penniless means without, so the word simply says without a penny.
normal.cn: penniless 里的后缀 -less 意为「没有」，所以这个词就是「没有一便士」。

normal.en: A penny-pinching person pinches every penny until it hurts, and the compound names the habit.
normal.cn: penny-pinching 的人把每一分钱都攥到发疼，这个复合词命名的正是这种习惯。

normal.en: A penny for your thoughts asks for a thought as if it were worth one small coin.
normal.cn: a penny for your thoughts 把你的想法当作只值一枚小硬币来索要。

abstract.en: A coin small enough to lose is also small enough to stand for every coin you do not have.
abstract.cn: 小到容易丢失的一枚硬币，也小到能代表你缺的每一分钱。

abstract.en: One word holding two plurals is a small lesson in how English separates the thing from its value.
abstract.cn: 一个词带着两个复数，正好说明英语如何把「东西」和「价值」分开。

abstract.en: The penny survives because a price needs a smallest step, and a language needs a word for almost nothing.
abstract.cn: penny 能留下来，因为价格需要一个最小刻度，语言也需要一个表示「几乎没有」的词。

examples.en: The newspaper costs two pounds and fifty pence.
examples.cn: 这份报纸卖两英镑五十便士。

examples.en: He emptied his pockets and counted the pennies.
examples.cn: 他把口袋掏空，数着一枚枚便士。

examples.en: She never spends a penny on herself.
examples.cn: 她从不为自己花一分钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喷你」——喷泉边掉出一枚小硬币，水花喷你一身；记住 penny 是便士、小硬币。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a coin, its value and its smallest-amount use; the two plurals carry the split between pieces and amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指硬币、又指币值，还用于「一分钱」；两个复数分别承担「一枚枚」和「金额」的分工。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the early coin name is Germanic and its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；早期的硬币名属日耳曼语，更早的来源不确定。

definition_zh: 养老金；退休金；津贴；发给…养老金
definition_en: a regular sum paid to someone who has stopped working, a similar allowance for other reasons, or to give such a payment to someone
core_image: 一只按月寄到的信封，装着固定的生活费
scene: 厂里的老会计到了退休年纪，人事把一份表格推到他面前。After forty years, he was pensioned off with a modest monthly income.
sceneCN: 这里是「发给…养老金、使退休」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为干了四十年后，他领着一笔不多的月钱被安排退休。

derivatives.zh: 由 pension 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「领养老金的人」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「有资格领取养老金的」
加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「养老金的；领取养老金的」

senses.title: Regular income after retirement
senses.definition: a sum of money paid regularly to a person who has retired from work
senses.definitionCN: 定期支付给已退休人员的钱
senses.example: She lives on a small state pension.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠一笔不多的国家养老金生活。
senses.why: Latin pensio began as a payment weighed out on a fixed measure, and that fixed measure is what makes the modern payment regular rather than earned hour by hour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pensio 最初指按固定份量称出来的付款，正是这种「固定份量」让今天的这笔钱按月发放，而不是按小时挣来。

senses.title: A similar allowance for other reasons
senses.definition: a regular payment made for injury, widowhood or long service rather than for retirement
senses.definitionCN: 因伤残、丧偶或长期服务而定期领取的钱，而不是因为退休
senses.example: The widow receives a pension from the state.
senses.exampleCN: 这位遗孀从国家领取抚恤金。
senses.why: Once the word meant a periodic payment rather than a wage, it could cover any fixed allowance, because the timing, not the reason, defines it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的不是工资而是定期付款，它就能覆盖任何固定补助，因为定义它的是发放的节奏，而不是发放的理由。

senses.title: To give someone a pension and end their work
senses.definition: to pay a pension to someone, usually when their working life is being brought to an end
senses.definitionCN: 向某人支付养老金，通常是在结束其职业生涯的时候
senses.example: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。
senses.why: The verb turns the payment into an act done to a person; the particle off adds the sense of being set aside from the active staff.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「付款」变成对某人做的动作；小品词 off 又添上「被从在职人员中挪开」的意思。

intro.en: Pension goes back to a Latin verb for hanging and weighing, whose noun came to mean a payment measured out at a fixed time.
intro.cn: pension 可上溯到拉丁语中表示悬挂与称重的动词，其名词后来指在固定时间量出来的付款。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh and pay out, because goods were weighed against metal on a balance.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂，也表示称重和付款，因为货物要在天平上与金属对量。

items.en: Pensio named a weighing and then a payment, the sum measured out at an agreed time.
items.cn: pensio 先指称量，后指付款，即在约定时间称量出来的那笔钱。

items.en: Old French took pension as a payment or rent and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把 pension 用作付款或租金，并在诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English pension meant a fixed regular payment, often for service or favour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pension 指固定定期付款，常因服务或恩惠而给。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the main sense to retirement income and grew a verb meaning to retire someone on such pay.
items.cn: 现代英语把主要义项收窄为退休收入，并长出「发养老金使某人退休」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the derived forms and other words on the Latin stem for hanging and weighing; the near-meaning group collects kinds of regular payment.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同一拉丁词干（悬挂、称重）上的其他词；近义组收各类定期付款。

entries.definition: Money paid regularly for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的定期支付的钱。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid every year, often for life.
entries.definitionCN: 每年支付的固定金额，常为终身。

entries.definition: Money paid by the state to people in need.
entries.definitionCN: 国家发给困难者的补助。

entries.definition: British term for a retirement pension scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指退休养老金制度。

normalIntro.en: The word hangs on a Latin verb for weighing and paying, and its family keeps the picture of a sum measured out at fixed times.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词挂在拉丁语表示称重与付款的动词上，同族词保留着「按固定时间量出一笔钱」的画面。

normal.en: Pendere means to weigh, so a pension is money that was once weighed out on a balance.
normal.cn: pendere 意为称重，所以养老金最初是天平上称出来的钱。

normal.en: Suspend and pendant share the same root: to hang, which is what a balance does before it settles.
normal.cn: suspend 与 pendant 同根，都是「悬挂」，这正是天平在稳定前的动作。

normal.en: Add -er and a pensioner is the person on the receiving end of the payment.
normal.cn: 加 -er，pensioner 就是收这笔钱的人。

normal.en: Pension off means to move someone onto a pension and out of the active list.
normal.cn: pension off 意为把某人转到养老金上、移出在职名单。

normal.en: Pension is the income; allowance is the wider word for any regular payment.
normal.cn: pension 是这笔收入本身；allowance 是更宽的词，指任何定期付款。

abstract.en: A pension is time turned into money: years of work are weighed and paid back month by month.
abstract.cn: 养老金是把时间换成了钱：多年的工作被称量，再按月还回来。

abstract.en: The word remembers a balance because retirement is an accounting of a whole working life.
abstract.cn: 这个词记着一架天平，因为退休是对一整段职业生涯的结算。

abstract.en: To be pensioned off is to be valued and set aside at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 被安排领养老金退休，是在同一刻既被计价、又被挪到一边。

examples.en: She lives on a small state pension.
examples.cn: 她靠一笔不多的国家养老金生活。

examples.en: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。

examples.en: His pension is paid directly into the bank.
examples.cn: 他的养老金直接打进银行账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盼薪」——退休以后每个月盼着那笔薪水到账；记住 pension 是养老金。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称重、付款）派生名词 pensio（称量、付款），经古法语 pension 进入英语；同族词多与「悬挂、称量」有关。

sensesIntro.en: One core payment, measured out at fixed times, divides into retirement income, other allowances, and the act of putting someone on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一笔按固定时间量出来的钱，分成退休收入、其他补助，以及「让某人领这笔钱」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope arriving every month with a fixed sum inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只按月寄到的信封，装着固定的生活费。

branches.en: a monthly payment after the last day at work
branches.cn: 最后一个工作日之后的月付

branches.en: a payment for injury or widowhood
branches.cn: 因伤残或丧偶而领的钱

branches.en: a manager being moved onto the retired list
branches.cn: 经理被转到退休名单

branches.en: from receiving the money to being retired on it
branches.cn: 从领这笔钱到因它而退休

branches.en: the same payment seen as income and as an action
branches.cn: 同一笔钱作为收入和作为动作

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb of weighing and paying, its noun, and English endings that name the person and the right.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示称重与付款的动词、它的名词，以及把人、把资格命名出来的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family hangs on pendere, to hang and to weigh, and its noun pensio, a payment measured out; English took the noun through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族挂在 pendere（悬挂、称重）与名词 pensio（量出来的付款）上；英语经法语借入的是名词。

definition_zh: 胡椒；胡椒粉；辣椒；撒胡椒粉
definition_en: a hot spice made from dried berries, the hollow fruit of related plants used as a vegetable, or to scatter this spice over food
core_image: 手指捻动小瓶，深色粉末簌簌落在食物上
scene: 灶台前，厨师把刚煎好的牛排放在案板上，手腕一抖，细粉落满表面。The chef peppered the steak and slid it onto the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「撒胡椒粉」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为厨师给牛排撒上胡椒，再把它滑进盘子。

由 pepper 与 mill 复合而成，义为「胡椒研磨器」

senses.title: The spice made from dried berries
senses.definition: a hot spice made from the dried berries of a tropical vine, used as a powder or in whole grains
senses.definitionCN: 由热带藤本植物的干果制成的辛辣香料，可磨成粉或整粒使用
senses.example: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
senses.exampleCN: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。
senses.why: Latin piper named the spice itself, and English kept it as a mass noun for the powder that is shaken over food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 piper 指的就是这种香料本身，英语把它保留为不可数名词，指撒在食物上的粉末。

senses.title: The hollow fruit eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the hollow fruit of plants in the same family, eaten as a vegetable in colours such as green, red and yellow
senses.definitionCN: 同科植物的中空果实，作为蔬菜食用，有绿、红、黄等颜色
senses.example: She stuffed the peppers with rice and baked them.
senses.exampleCN: 她把米饭塞进辣椒里烤熟。
senses.why: The spice and the vegetable come from the same plant family, so one name covers both, and cooks count the vegetable one by one.
senses.whyCN: 香料和蔬菜来自同一科植物，于是一个名称覆盖两者；而做菜时蔬菜是一颗颗数的。

senses.title: To scatter pepper over food
senses.definition: to shake pepper or a similar powder over food before eating or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 在烹调或进食前把胡椒或类似粉末撒在食物上
senses.example: He peppered the eggs and handed me the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 他给鸡蛋撒上胡椒，把盘子递给我。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: the powder leaves the shaker in small specks and lands on whatever lies below.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词动起来：粉末从瓶里成小点落下，落在下面的东西上。

senses.title: To cover with many small things
senses.definition: to cover a surface with many small marks or objects, or to hit someone with a rapid stream of questions, shots or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 用许多小点或小物布满一个表面，或向某人连续发出问题、射击或批评
senses.example: Reporters peppered her with questions as she left the court.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。
senses.why: Once pepper is a shower of specks, the verb can describe anything arriving that way, so words and bullets behave like grains of powder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦胡椒被看成一阵密集的小点，这个动词就能描写任何以这种方式到来的东西，于是话语和子弹都像粉末颗粒。

intro.en: Pepper travelled west along trade routes, from an Indic name for long pepper through Greek and Latin into Old English.
intro.cn: pepper 沿着贸易路线西行，从印度方面表示长胡椒的名称，经希腊语、拉丁语进入古英语。

items.en: Sanskrit pippali named long pepper, and the deeper origin of the word is generally thought to lie outside Indo-European, possibly in a Dravidian language.
items.cn: 梵语 pippali 指长胡椒，这个词更早的来源一般认为在印欧语之外，可能来自某种达罗毗荼语。

items.en: Greek took the word as peperi, and Greek traders carried both the spice and the name westward.
items.cn: 希腊语把它写作 peperi，希腊商人把香料和名称一起带向西方。

items.en: Latin piper named the spice, and Roman cooks used it so heavily that it became a common item of trade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 piper 指胡椒，罗马厨师用得极多，使它成了常见的贸易货品。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin word as pipor, and the spelling later shifted to pepper.
items.cn: 古英语借入拉丁词写作 pipor，后来拼写演变为 pepper。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spice and the vegetable under one word and uses the verb for any dense shower of things.
items.cn: 现代英语用同一个词表示香料和蔬菜，并用动词描写任何密集袭来的一阵东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derived words and compounds built on the spice name; the near-meaning group collects other seasonings and members of the pepper family.
note.cn: 形近组收由这一香料名构成的派生词与复合词；近义组收其他调味料以及胡椒家族的成员。

entries.definition: Tasting of pepper, or quick to anger.
entries.definitionCN: 有胡椒味的；易怒的。

entries.definition: A single dried berry of the pepper plant.
entries.definitionCN: 胡椒的整粒干果。

entries.definition: A small device for grinding peppercorns.
entries.definitionCN: 研磨胡椒粒的小器具。

entries.definition: A mint plant with a strong cool taste.
entries.definitionCN: 一种薄荷，名字取自胡椒般的刺激味道，与胡椒并非同一种植物。

entries.definition: A small hot pepper used in cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 做菜用的小而辣的辣椒。

entries.definition: A dried plant substance used to flavour food.
entries.definitionCN: 用于给食物调味的干燥植物性香料。

entries.definition: The botanical name for peppers and their fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 辣椒属及其果实的植物学名称。

entries.definition: Salt, pepper or spices added to improve flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 为提味而加的盐、胡椒或香料。

normalIntro.en: The word keeps a Latin spice name on top of an older Indic root, and its family stays close to the kitchen and to the idea of many small specks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在更古老的印度词根之上保存了一个拉丁香料名，同族词始终贴近厨房，也贴近「许多小颗粒」这个意象。

normal.en: Piper is the Latin name, and the English word keeps the double p of the original.
normal.cn: piper 是拉丁名，英语词保留了原词的双写 p。

normal.en: The spice is uncountable, so you say some pepper, while the vegetable is countable, so you say two peppers.
normal.cn: 香料不可数，说 some pepper；蔬菜可数，说 two peppers。

normal.en: Peppery adds -y, the suffix that turns a noun into a quality, so the word means full of pepper.
normal.cn: peppery 加 -y，这个后缀把名词变成性质，所以词义是「充满胡椒的」。

normal.en: A peppercorn is one grain, which is why a mill grinds corns rather than powder.
normal.cn: peppercorn 是一粒，所以研磨器磨的是颗粒而不是粉末。

normal.en: Pepper with questions borrows the picture of many small grains hitting a surface at once.
normal.cn: pepper with questions 借用了许多小颗粒同时打在一个表面上的画面。

abstract.en: A spice and a vegetable share one name because both come from the same family, and language often prefers the family resemblance over precision.
abstract.cn: 香料和蔬菜共用一个名字，因为两者同科；语言常常更看重亲缘相似，而不是精确区分。

abstract.en: To pepper someone with questions is to treat words as if they were grains thrown by the handful.
abstract.cn: 用问题 pepper 某人，就是把话语当成一把把撒出去的颗粒。

abstract.en: The word travelled from a Sanskrit name for long pepper to a Latin trade good to an English kitchen, carried by the same appetite.
abstract.cn: 这个词从梵语的长胡椒之名，走到拉丁语的贸易货，再走到英语的厨房，靠的是同一种胃口。

examples.en: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
examples.cn: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。

examples.en: The garden is full of green and red peppers.
examples.cn: 园子里长满了青椒和红椒。

examples.en: Journalists peppered her with questions as she left the court.
examples.cn: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍拍」——往牛排上拍拍胡椒瓶，粉末落下来；记住 pepper 是胡椒。

root: 古英语 pipor 借自拉丁语 piper，更早可追到希腊语 peperi 与梵语 pippali（长胡椒）；同族词多与这种香料有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the spice, the vegetable from the same family, the act of scattering it, and any dense shower of small things.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指香料、同科的蔬菜、撒粉的动作，以及任何密集落下的小东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand shaking a small jar so that dark powder falls onto food.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指捻动小瓶，深色粉末簌簌落在食物上。

branches.en: a mill grinding dried berries into powder
branches.cn: 研磨器把干果磨成粉

branches.en: a hollow red fruit stuffed with rice
branches.cn: 塞满米饭的中空红果

branches.en: a hand shaking powder over a steak
branches.cn: 手把粉末撒在牛排上

branches.en: questions arriving like thrown grains
branches.cn: 问题像撒出的颗粒一样袭来

branches.en: from scattering powder to scattering words
branches.cn: 从撒粉末到撒话语

intro.en: The word is a Latin spice name carried into English, and its family grows through English compounds and suffixes around the kitchen.
intro.cn: 这个词是传入英语的拉丁香料名，同族词围绕厨房，靠英语的复合与后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word piper is the direct source of the English name, and it came to Latin from Greek, which took it from an Indic word for long pepper.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 piper 是英语名称的直接来源；它由希腊语传入拉丁语，而希腊语又借自印度方面表示长胡椒的词。

items.meaning: full of pepper, sharp in taste

definition_zh: 每；每一；按照；根据；经由；由
definition_en: used to show how much of something belongs to each unit, such as each person, hour or kilometre; also according to, and by way of
core_image: 一把量杯上刻着一格一格的刻度，每一格都装着同样多的东西
scene: 清晨的渡口挂着木牌，船夫按人头收过渡费，来一个人收一次。The ferryman charges five yuan per passenger before the boat leaves the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 per 是「每、每一」（第 1 个义项：按单位逐一计算份量）；句意为开船之前，船夫向每位乘客收五元。画面的重点是刻度式的一份一份。

derivatives.zh: 由 per 与拉丁语 centum（百）组合而成，义为「百分比」
在 percent 后加名词后缀 -age，义为「百分比；比例」
拉丁短语 per capita（按人头）整体进入英语，义为「人均的」

senses.title: For each unit
senses.definition: used to state how much of something corresponds to one person, hour, kilometre or other unit
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明每一个人、每一小时、每一公里等对应多少量
senses.example: The room costs eighty dollars per night.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间每晚八十美元。
senses.why: Latin per already worked in distributive phrases such as per diem, so English simply kept that rhythm: one measured portion for every single unit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per 早已用于表示分配的说法，如按日计算，所以英语直接沿用了这种节奏：每一个单位都配一份量。

senses.title: According to
senses.definition: used to mean in accordance with what someone has said, asked for or decided
senses.definitionCN: 表示与某人的说法、要求或决定相一致
senses.example: Per your request, the meeting has been moved to Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 按照你的要求，会议已改到星期五。
senses.why: If something reaches you through a person, that person becomes the source of the instruction, so through slides into according to, the way a message is passed on in an office.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是经某个人传到你这儿的，那个人就成了指令的来源，于是「经由」滑向「按照」，就像办公室里逐层转达的口信。

senses.title: By way of
senses.definition: used to name the person or the means through which something is sent, carried or done
senses.definitionCN: 用于指出某物经谁之手、或以什么方式送出、运走或完成
senses.example: The documents were sent per courier.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件由快递员送出。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the Latin word: movement through a channel, whether a road, a hand or a service, and English kept it for post, fax and courier.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁词最古老的一层意思：沿着某个通道穿过，通道可以是道路、一只手或一项服务，英语把它保留在邮寄、传真与快递的说法里。

senses.title: In every hundred
senses.definition: used in the phrase per cent to express a rate measured out of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 用于 per cent 这一短语，表示以一百为基数计算的比率
senses.example: Prices rose by three per cent last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格上涨了三个百分点。
senses.why: Per cent joins per with Latin centum, a hundred, and the counting frame does the rest: so many units out of every hundred.
senses.whyCN: per cent 把 per 与拉丁语 centum（一百）拼在一起，剩下的交给计数框架完成：每一百当中占多少。

intro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage, and English took it over both as a word of route and as a word of counting.
intro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，英语既把它当作「路线词」，也把它当作「计数词」接收下来。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- carried the idea of forward motion and passing through, and forms built on it appear in many branches of the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 per- 带有「向前、穿过」的意思，由它构成的词形出现在语系的许多分支里。

items.en: Latin per meant through, across or by means of, and it could also mark the person through whom something happened.
items.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为穿过、横越、凭借，也可以标出事情是经谁发生的。

items.en: In phrases such as per diem and per capita, the word moved from place to share, meaning for each day and for each head.
items.cn: 在 per diem、per capita 这类短语里，这个词从「位置」转到「分配」，意为每天、每人。

items.en: English borrowed the counting use first in trade, law and household accounts, where rates were quoted per dozen, per acre and per year.
items.cn: 英语先在贸易、法律与家庭账目里借用这种计数用法，报价写作每打、每英亩、每年。

items.en: Modern English adds as per and per cent, so one small word now marks a rate, a source and a percentage at once.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 as per 与 per cent，于是同一个小词同时标记比率、来源与百分比。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words and phrases built on the same Latin preposition; the near-meaning group gathers the determiners and prepositions that divide or route things.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁介词上的词与短语；近义组收表示分配与途径的限定词、介词。

entries.definition: A word for a rate out of a hundred, built from per plus Latin centum.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per 与拉丁语 centum（百）构成的词，表示百分之几。

entries.definition: The two-word British form of the same idea, still common in British writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的两词英式写法，在英式文本里仍很常见。

entries.definition: To keep going firmly, built on per- plus a Latin verb meaning to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per- 加表示「站立」的拉丁动词构成，义为坚持。

entries.definition: To spread through every part of something, with per- meaning through.
entries.definitionCN: per- 表示穿过，故义为弥漫、遍及。

entries.definition: Every one of two or more things, taken one at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或更多事物中的每一个，逐一来看。

entries.definition: All the members of a group, considered one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 一组中的全部成员，逐个来看。

entries.definition: By going through a place, or by using a particular method.
entries.definitionCN: 经由某地，或使用某种方法。

entries.definition: Used to name the person or the method that does something.
entries.definitionCN: 用于指出做某事的人或方法。

normalIntro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage, and every English use keeps either the route or the counting beat built into it.
normalIntro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，英语的每种用法都保留了它内含的路线或计数节拍。

normal.en: Per is the Latin word for through, so anything sent per someone passes through that person's hands.
normal.cn: per 在拉丁语里是「穿过」，所以经某人转交的东西要先过那个人的手。

normal.en: Per cent is per plus centum, the Latin word for a hundred: so many in every hundred.
normal.cn: per cent 是 per 加拉丁语 centum（一百），即每一百当中占多少。

normal.en: Per capita joins per with capita, the Latin word for heads: one share for each head.
normal.cn: per capita 把 per 与拉丁语 capita（头）连起来：按人头各分一份。

normal.en: As per is the business formula for according to, and it appears in letters, notices and instructions.
normal.cn: as per 是商业文书里表示「按照」的固定说法，常见于信件、通告与说明。

normal.en: Per hour, per night and per person all keep one frame: a fixed amount repeated for each unit.
normal.cn: per hour、per night、per person 都保持同一个框架：固定的量按单位重复。

abstract.en: A ruler scored with equal spaces is the clearest picture of per: the same amount repeated at every mark.
abstract.cn: 一把刻着等距刻度的尺子最能说明 per：每一格都是同样的量。

abstract.en: The word began as motion through space and ended as a way of splitting amounts, a journey from road to ledger.
abstract.cn: 这个词从空间中的穿行开始，最后成为分配数量的工具，一路从道路走到账簿。

abstract.en: Because per stands between an amount and a unit, it forces the speaker to say what the amount is measured against.
abstract.cn: 因为 per 夹在数量与单位之间，它逼着说话人交代这个量是拿什么来衡量的。

examples.en: The room costs eighty dollars per night.
examples.cn: 这个房间每晚八十美元。

examples.en: Per your request, the meeting has been moved to Friday.
examples.cn: 按照你的要求，会议已改到星期五。

examples.en: Prices rose by three per cent last month.
examples.cn: 上个月价格上涨了三个百分点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼」——一桶水泼出去，每处都沾到一点；用它记住 per 是「每」。

root: 拉丁语介词 per（穿过、经由、每）直接进入英语；同族词多与「穿过、彻底」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a quantity measured against a unit; from that counting frame grow the ideas of source, route and percentage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以一个单位为基准的量」；来源、途径与百分比三个意思都从这个计数框架里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measuring cup marked with equal lines, one portion standing for every line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把量杯上刻着一格一格的线，每一条线代表同样的一份。

branches.cn: 按人头收费的售票窗口

branches.en: a price tag that shows both a rate and a share
branches.cn: 同时标着单价与百分比的价签

branches.en: a notice that opens with the words of the person who asked
branches.cn: 以对方要求开头的通知

branches.en: a parcel passing from one pair of hands to another
branches.cn: 在一双双手之间转交的包裹

branches.en: a chart that cuts a total into a hundred parts
branches.cn: 把总量切成一百份的图表

intro.en: Per is a Latin preposition of passage; the English forms around it are mostly phrases that share the same counting frame.
intro.cn: per 是拉丁语中表示穿行的介词，围绕它的英语形式多是共用同一计数框架的短语。

latinIntro.en: Both halves of the percentage words come from Latin: per and centum are securely attested and their meanings are not in doubt.
latinIntro.cn: 百分比一族的两半都来自拉丁语：per 与 centum 均有可靠记载，含义没有争议。

definition_zh: 察觉；感知；注意到；认为；视为；领会
definition_en: to become aware of something through the senses or the mind, or to regard something in a particular way
core_image: 一张网彻底罩住外界送来的信息，把它整个抓住
scene: 盲人用手杖轻敲地面。The tip of the cane touched a raised edge before anyone could see it, and he could perceive the step under his feet.
sceneCN: 这里 perceive 是「凭感官察觉」（第 1 个义项：用感官接住它）；句意：手杖的尖端在任何人都还没看见之前就碰到了凸起的边缘，他凭触觉察觉到了脚下的台阶。图中可辨识物件：白色手杖、台阶边缘、导盲犬、行人、地面纹理；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有洞察力的；感知敏锐的

senses.title: Catch it through the senses
senses.definition: to become aware of something through sight, hearing, smell, touch, or taste
senses.definitionCN: 通过视觉、听觉、嗅觉、触觉或味觉意识到某物
senses.example: She perceived a faint smell of smoke in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到走廊里有一丝烟味。
senses.why: Latin percipere joins per- 'thoroughly' to capere 'to take'. Perception is a taking hold: the senses reach out and grasp what the world offers, which is why the word works for every sense at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 percipere 把 per-“彻底”与 capere“拿取”结合。感知就是抓住：感官伸出去，把外界送来的东西握在手里，因此这个词能同时用于所有感官。

senses.title: Notice a small change
senses.definition: to notice something subtle that might easily be missed
senses.definitionCN: 注意到容易被忽略的细微之处
senses.example: The doctor perceived a slight change in his breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生察觉到他呼吸的细微变化。
senses.why: The 'thorough' in per- explains why the word often implies effort: the change is small, and the observer has to take hold of it before it disappears.
senses.whyCN: per- 里的“彻底”解释了为什么这个词常隐含用力：变化很小，观察者必须在它消失之前把它抓住。

senses.title: Realize: come to know
senses.definition: to come to realize or understand a fact, often gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐意识到或明白一个事实
senses.example: I perceived that the plan would not work.
senses.exampleCN: 我意识到这个计划行不通。
senses.why: Mental grasp uses the same hand as physical grasp. Once the mind closes on a fact, the fact is held, and English lets perceive cover that inner taking as well.
senses.whyCN: 心智的把握与身体的抓取用同一只手。一旦心思合拢在一个事实上，这个事实就被握住了，英语也让 perceive 覆盖这种内在的拿取。

senses.title: Regard it as: perceive as
senses.definition: to regard or classify something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定方式看待或归类某事物
senses.example: Many voters perceive the tax as unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 许多选民认为这项税不公平。
senses.why: What you take hold of is not only the object but the category you put it in. The construction perceive as marks that act of placing, which is why it dominates in opinion research.
senses.whyCN: 你抓住的不只是对象，还包括你把它放进的那个类别。perceive as 这一结构标记“归类放置”的动作，因此它在民意研究中占主导。

senses.title: Grasp a meaning
senses.definition: to understand the meaning or significance of something said, written, or shown
senses.definitionCN: 理解所说、所写或所展示之物的含义或意义
senses.example: He perceived the irony in her remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他领会了她话里的讽刺。
senses.why: Meaning is not visible on the surface of words. To perceive it is to take hold of something that is implied rather than displayed, and this sense has been central since the Latin verb also meant 'to understand'.
senses.whyCN: 意义并不写在词语表面。领会它就是抓住某种被暗示而非被展示的东西；自拉丁语动词兼有“理解”义以来，这一义项一直是核心。

senses.title: Be seen in a certain light
senses.definition: in the passive, to be viewed or judged in a particular way by others
senses.definitionCN: 被动式中，被他人以特定方式看待或评判
senses.example: The reform is widely perceived as a retreat.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革被普遍视为一种退却。
senses.why: Perception is not only what an individual grasps but what a public settles on. In the passive the word names a shared judgement, which is why it appears so often in political and media language.
senses.whyCN: 感知不只是个人抓住什么，也包括公众最终认定什么。被动式中，这个词命名的是一种共同判断，因此它频繁出现在政治与媒体语言里。

senses.title: Perception as a field of study
senses.definition: in psychology, the process by which sensory input is detected, organized, and given meaning
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，感官输入被检测、组织并赋予意义的过程
senses.example: The study tests how colour perception changes with age.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验颜色知觉如何随年龄变化。
senses.why: Psychology separates the raw signal from the interpreted result. The word then names the whole pipeline from sensation to meaning, and perception becomes a countable object of experiment.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把原始信号与解释后的结果分开。这个词于是命名从感觉到意义的整条流水线，perception 也变成实验中可计数的对象。

senses.title: Perceive without senses: grasp by intuition
senses.titleCN: 不靠感官的领会：直觉把握
senses.definition: in older or religious usage, to apprehend a truth directly, without sensory evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老或宗教的用法中，不经感官证据而直接把握一个真理
senses.example: The mystics claimed to perceive a unity behind all things.
senses.exampleCN: 神秘主义者声称领悟到万物背后的统一。
senses.why: If perception is a taking hold, it does not have to happen through the body. Religious and philosophical writers extended it to the mind's direct grasp of truths, keeping the hand and dropping the senses.
senses.whyCN: 如果感知就是抓住，那么它不必通过身体发生。宗教与哲学作者把它扩展到心智对真理的直接把握：保留那只手，放下感官。

intro.en: Perceive is Latin in origin and replaced an Old English verb. Its root is capere 'to take', not the cent- of percentage: the shared per- is a prefix, not a common root.
intro.cn: perceive 源自拉丁语，取代了一个古英语动词。它的词根是 capere“拿取”，而不是 percentage 的 cent-：两者共有的 per- 只是前缀，不是共同词根。

items.en: Perceive is recorded, from the Anglo-French stem parceif-, from Old French perçoivre, from Latin percipere.
items.cn: perceive 记录于 1300 年前后，来自盎格鲁-法语词干 parceif-，再上溯古法语 perçoivre 与拉丁语 percipere。

items.en: Percipere means 'to obtain, grasp, understand'. It joins per- 'thoroughly' to capere 'to take, seize'. The image is a complete taking hold, not a passing look.
items.cn: percipere 意为“获得、抓住、理解”。它把 per-“彻底”与 capere“拿取、抓住”结合。画面是“彻底握住”，而不是“瞥一眼”。

items.en: Capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp', the source also of capture, accept, and capable. The asterisk marks a reconstructed root.
items.cn: capere 上溯原始印欧语 *kap-“抓取”，也是 capture、accept、capable 的来源。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: Perceive displaces the Old English verbs ongietan 'to grasp, understand' and gefredan 'to feel'. The newcomers from French took over the mental as well as the sensory field.
items.cn: perceive 取代古英语动词 ongietan“抓住、理解”与 gefredan“感觉”。这些来自法语的新词同时接管了心智与感官两个领域。

items.en: The noun perception is fixed in philosophy, then in psychology, where it names the processing of sensory input. The passive 'is perceived as' becomes standard in public opinion language.
items.cn: 名词 perception 先在哲学中定型，后在心理学中命名感官输入的处理过程。被动式“is perceived as”成为民意语言的标准说法。

note.en: The first group is per- words with different roots; the second compares verbs of noticing and judging.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 per-、但词根不同的词；第二组比较表示“注意与判断”的动词。

entries.definition: to keep something safe or unchanged. It looks close but its root is servare 'to keep', not capere.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某物、使其不变。外形相近，但词根是 servare“保存”，不是 capere。

entries.definition: deliberately turning away from what is right or reasonable. Its root is vertere 'to turn', so it is a turning aside, not a grasping.
entries.definitionCN: 故意背离正确或合理之事。其词根是 vertere“转”，因此是“转开”，不是“抓住”。

entries.definition: to keep going despite difficulty. Its root is severus 'strict, serious', a different family from capere.
entries.definitionCN: 遇到困难仍坚持下去。其词根是 severus“严格、严肃”，与 capere 属不同词族。

entries.definition: able to be noticed. It is built on the same perception stem, so it is a true relative, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: 能被察觉的。它建立在同一个 perception 词干上，是真正的同族词，而不是形近词。

entries.definition: to become aware of something by paying attention. It is more casual and often momentary; perceive can imply a fuller grasp.
entries.definitionCN: 通过注意而意识到某物。它更随意、常为瞬间；perceive 可暗示更完整的把握。

entries.definition: to become aware of something without being able to say exactly why. It stresses intuition; perceive can be sensory or reasoned.
entries.definitionCN: 说不出确切理由地意识到某事。它强调直觉；perceive 可以是感官的，也可以是推理的。

entries.definition: to look on or consider in a particular way. It matches the 'perceive as' sense but lacks the sensory meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式看待或考虑。它对应“perceive as”这一义项，但没有感官义。

entries.definition: to see or understand something that is not obvious, especially a difference. It stresses discrimination, while perceive stresses awareness.
entries.definitionCN: 看出或理解不明显之物，尤指差别。它强调分辨，而 perceive 强调觉察。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on per- and taking, then three abstract images about grasping what is not obvious.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 per- 与“拿取”的挂钩，再用三个关于“抓住不明显之物”的抽象画面。

normal.en: per- means thoroughly, -ceive comes from capere 'take'. To perceive is to take something in completely.
normal.cn: per- 是“彻底”，-ceive 来自 capere“拿取”。perceive 就是把某物完整地拿进来。

normal.en: receive, deceive, perceive all hide capere: each is a different way of taking.
normal.cn: receive、deceive、perceive 都藏着 capere：每一种都是不同方式的“拿”。

normal.en: perceive as: the 'as' is the box you put the thing into. You take it and file it under a label.
normal.cn: perceive as：那个 as 就是你把它放进去的盒子。你抓住它，再贴上一个标签归档。

normal.en: A blind person's cane perceives the step before the eyes do: the hand takes hold first.
normal.cn: 盲人的手杖先于眼睛感知到台阶：手先抓住。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with percent: perceive has a c-e-i-v-e root of taking, while percent counts hundreds.
normal.cn: 别和 percent 混：perceive 的 c-e-i-v-e 是“拿取”词根，percent 数的是“百”。

abstract.en: Perception is never passive: to perceive is to select, and selection is already interpretation.
abstract.cn: 感知从不被动：感知就是选择，而选择已经是解释。

abstract.en: What a group perceives becomes real in its consequences, even if the perception is wrong.
abstract.cn: 一个群体所感知的东西会通过后果变成现实，即使这个感知是错的。

abstract.en: To perceive a meaning is to take hold of something no one can hand you.
abstract.cn: 领会一层含义，就是抓住一件没有人能直接交给你的东西。

examples.en: The sensor perceives motion and turns on the light.
examples.cn: 传感器感知到动作，随即打开灯。

examples.en: Tourists often perceive the city as safer than residents do.
examples.cn: 游客常常比本地居民更觉得这座城市安全。

examples.en: It took her a moment to perceive why the room had gone quiet.
examples.cn: 她花了一会儿才领会房间为何安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.note: per- 记成“彻底”，-ceive 记成“拿”（capere）：把外界的东西整个拿进来，就是感知。
dict_mnemonic.text: per（彻底）+ ceive（拿取）→ 彻底抓住 → 察觉、感知、领会、视为

root: 拉丁 percipere“抓住、领会”＝per（彻底）+ capere（拿取，原始印欧语 *kap-）→ 古法语 perçoivre → 英语 perceive。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the senses themselves to subtle noticing, to realizing, to the category you put a thing in, to grasping meaning, to being seen by a public, to the science of perception, and finally to a grasp that needs no senses at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从感官本身开始，转到细微察觉、意识到、把事物放进某个类别、领会含义、被公众看待、作为研究对象的知觉，最后落到完全不需要感官的把握。

core.en: A hand closing completely around what the world holds out
core.cn: 一只手彻底合拢，握住外界递来的东西

branches.en: Sensory grasp: what the body detects, and how psychology models that detection.
branches.cn: 感官把握：身体检测到什么，以及心理学如何建模这一检测。

branches.en: Small signal to inner fact: noticing a change, then realizing what it means.
branches.cn: 从小信号到内在事实：察觉变化，然后意识到它意味着什么。

branches.en: Being placed: in the passive, someone is seen in a certain light.
branches.cn: 被放置：被动式中，某人被以某种眼光看待。

branches.en: Meaning without a surface: reading irony, and grasping a truth without senses.
branches.cn: 没有表面的意义：读出讽刺，以及不靠感官把握真理。

branches.en: The label: the same grasp that takes the thing files it under a category.
branches.cn: 标签：抓住事物的同一动作，也把它归入某个类别。

intro.en: Perceive's family centres on the -ceive / -cept stem from capere: perception, perceptive, perceptible, and the modern misperceive.
intro.cn: perceive 的词族以 capere 而来的 -ceive / -cept 词干为中心：perception、perceptive、perceptible，以及现代的 misperceive。

latinIntro.en: Latin percipere and its noun perceptio are the direct sources. Capere 'to take' supplies the stem; per- adds the idea of thoroughness, not a separate root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 percipere 及其名词 perceptio 是直接来源。capere“拿取”提供词干；per- 增加“彻底”之意，并不是另一个词根。

items.meaning: to become aware of, grasp, or regard
items.example: We perceived a change in the tone.

items.meaning: awareness; the process of perceiving; a view

items.meaningCN: 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
items.example: A perceptive reader spots the hint.
items.exampleCN: 敏锐的读者会看出那个暗示。
有一段能察觉到的停顿。

items.meaning: in a way that can be noticed

items.example: People misperceive the risk of rare events.
items.exampleCN: 人们会错估罕见事件的风险。

items.example: The perceiver's position shapes the report.
items.exampleCN: 感知者的位置塑造了这份报告。

items.example: Capere is the root of capture and accept.
items.exampleCN: capere 是 capture 与 accept 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Percipere is the direct source of perceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: percipere 是 perceive 的直接来源。
perceptio 是英语 perception 的基础。
capere 提供 perceive 中的 -ceive。

latinEntries.example: Perceptivus is the base of English perceptive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: perceptivus 是英语 perceptive 的基础。

definition_zh: 百分比；百分之……
definition_en: one part in every hundred; expressed in hundredths
core_image: 把整体切成一百份，取其中若干份的比例尺
scene: 商场周年庆，店员指着海报向顾客说明折扣幅度。The shop offered a discount of twenty percent on all shoes during the anniversary sale.
sceneCN: 这里 percent 是「百分比」（第 1 个义项：每一百份中的份额）；句意是周年庆期间所有鞋子打八折。

derivatives.zh: percent 加名词后缀 -age 构成，指「百分比；比例；比率」
percent 加 -ile 构成统计学术语，指「百分位数」

senses.title: A part of a hundred
senses.titleCN: 百分比；每一百份中的份额
senses.definition: one part in or for every hundred; a rate expressed in hundredths
senses.definitionCN: 每一百份中的一份或若干份；以百分数表示的比率
senses.example: Ten percent of the students failed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之十的学生没通过考试。
senses.why: Latin per centum literally means for each hundred, so the word itself fixes the whole at one hundred.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per centum 字面意思是「每一百」，所以这个词本身就把整体锁定为一百份。

senses.title: Percentage in general
senses.definition: a share or proportion of a whole, used loosely without a specific number
senses.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分或比例，泛指时不带具体数字
senses.example: A large percent of his income goes to rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他收入的很大一部分用于房租。
senses.why: When the hundred-part scale becomes a loose share of a whole, the concrete measure turns into an ordinary proportion.
senses.whyCN: 当一百份的刻度被泛化成整体的份额，具体的度量就变成普通的「比例」。

intro.en: Percent is a compressed Latin phrase that became an everyday English noun.
intro.cn: percent 是一个被压缩成日常名词的拉丁语短语。

items.en: The phrase per centum meant for each hundred, combining per (through, by) and centum (hundred).
items.cn: 拉丁短语 per centum 意为「每一百」，由 per（通过、按）和 centum（百）构成。

items.en: In commercial and tax records of medieval Europe, per centum was the standard way to state rates and interest.
items.cn: 中世纪欧洲的商业与税赋记录中，per centum 是表示利率、税率的标准写法。

items.en: Italian merchants used per cento, a shortened form, in account books of trading cities.
items.cn: 意大利商人在账簿中使用缩短的形式 per cento。

items.en: French adopted pour cent, keeping the same structure as business and finance spread.
items.cn: 随着商业金融扩散，法语吸收为 pour cent，结构不变。

items.en: English took over the phrase as per cent in the sixteenth century; the solid spelling percent arose in American usage and is now standard in the United States.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收短语 per cent；连写 percent 起于美式用法，如今是美国的标准拼法。

note.en: Words nearby percent differ in spelling, source, or range of use.
note.cn: 与 percent 相近的词在拼写、来源或使用范围上有差别。

entries.definition: a rate or proportion per hundred, or a share of a whole
entries.definitionCN: percentage 与 percent 同根，加后缀 -age，指百分比或整体中的份额

entries.definition: a value below which a given percentage of data falls, used in statistics
entries.definitionCN: percentile 同根，是统计学术语「百分位数」

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years, from Latin centum
entries.definitionCN: century 共享拉丁词根 centum（百），指一百年，与百分比无直接关系

entries.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole, not fixed to one hundred
entries.definitionCN: proportion 泛指部分与整体的比例，不固定为一百份

entries.definition: a measure of change or frequency, often per unit of time
entries.definitionCN: rate 指变化或频率的比率，常按单位时间计

entries.definition: a relation between two amounts shown by division, written as a:b
entries.definitionCN: ratio 指两个量之间的比值，写成 a:b，不限于百分制

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built from the Latin source and real usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于拉丁词源与真实用法的记忆锚点。

normal.en: per centum = for each hundred: percent literally pins the whole at one hundred.
normal.cn: per centum = 每一百：percent 字面就把整体锁定为一百。

normal.en: per- means through or by, as in perfect and permanent.
normal.cn: 前缀 per- 表示「通过、按」，同 perfect、permanent 中的 per-。

normal.en: -cent comes from centum (hundred), also seen in century and centimeter.
normal.cn: 词根 cent 来自 centum（百），也出现在 century、centimeter。

normal.en: The symbol % grew from an Italian scribal shorthand of per cento.
normal.cn: 符号 % 由意大利文书写的 per cento 缩写演变而来。

normal.en: Collocations run in fixed patterns: ten percent, a large percent of, increase by percent.
normal.cn: 搭配有固定套路：ten percent、a large percent of、increase by percent。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into one hundred slices; percent names how many slices you take.
abstract.cn: 想象一块蛋糕切成一百份，percent 说的就是你拿几份。

abstract.en: Think of a ruler whose whole length is always one hundred; percent is the reading on it.
abstract.cn: 把 percent 想成一把总长恒为一百的刻度尺上的读数。

abstract.en: Feel the crowd split into hundred tiny groups, each group one percent of the whole.
abstract.cn: 把人群分成一百个小组，每小组就是整体的百分之一。

examples.en: About sixty percent of the class joined the English club.
examples.cn: 班上大约百分之六十的学生加入了英语社团。

examples.en: Prices rose by five percent last year.
examples.cn: 去年价格上涨了百分之五。

examples.en: The chart shows the percent of time each device spends online.
examples.cn: 图表显示每台设备联网时间的百分比。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼森特」——把整锅汤泼成一百勺，泼出去几勺就是百分之几；谐音只助记，词源仍是拉丁语 per centum。

root: 拉丁语短语 per centum（每一百）：per-（按、通过）+ centum（百）；centum 同根词有 century、centimeter、centipede。

sensesIntro.en: From an exact hundred-part measure to a loose share of a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 从精确的百份刻度到泛指的整体份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole cut into one hundred equal parts
core.cn: 核心意象：整体被切成一百等份

branches.en: The fixed hundred-part scale gives the exact measure
branches.cn: 固定的一百份刻度给出精确度量（义项 01）

branches.en: Each slice of the hundred is a share
branches.cn: 一百份中的一份就是份额（义项 01）

branches.en: Loosened from numbers, the scale names any proportion
branches.cn: 脱离具体数字后泛指比例（义项 02）

branches.en: Shops and taxes use the scale for discounts and rates
branches.cn: 商店与税收用这个刻度表示折扣与税率（义项 01）

branches.en: Reports and statistics convert everything into the hundred scale
branches.cn: 报告与统计把一切换算成百分刻度（义项 01、02）

intro.en: Percent is built from two Latin pieces, and both keep working across the vocabulary.
intro.cn: percent 由两个拉丁构件构成，两者在整个词汇系统中都持续起作用。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives that carry the same pieces per- or cent-.
latinIntro.cn: 携带 per- 或 cent- 同一构件的拉丁同源词。

items.exampleCN: 拉丁前缀 per-，见 per centum、per person

items.example: centum meant one hundred in classical Latin
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词根 centum 在古典拉丁语中指一百
短语压缩成名词，见 ten percent of the total

items.meaning: a rate per hundred; a share

items.exampleCN: percent 加 -ile 的统计学术语
词根 cent- 构成的世纪名词
词缀 centi-（百分之一）+ meter

items.example: a centipede ran across the floor

definition_zh: 百分比；百分率；占比；按比例的分成；百分点；（口语）好处
definition_en: a rate or share expressed per hundred; also a proportion of a whole, a commission, and informally, an advantage
core_image: 一条被切成一百格的长条，其中若干格被涂上颜色
scene: 教室墙上贴着一条一百格的长条，三十格涂成橙色。The teacher pointed at the coloured squares and said that thirty out of one hundred was the percentage she wanted them to remember.
sceneCN: 这里 percentage 是「百分比」（第 1 个义项：以百为基数的比率）；句意：老师指着涂色的格子说，一百格里的三十格就是她要学生记住的百分比。图中可辨识物件：一百格长条、橙色涂格、白色空格、教鞭、数字标签；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 百分点（两个百分比之间的差）
每百；百分之（英式分写形式）

senses.title: A rate per hundred
senses.definition: a number or rate expressed as a fraction of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 以一百为分母表示的数值或比率
senses.example: Write the answer as a percentage rather than a decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案写成百分比，而不是小数。
senses.why: Percent is Latin per centum, 'by the hundred'. The -age suffix turns that phrase into a noun of rate, so a percentage is literally the result of counting how many parts there are in every hundred.
senses.whyCN: percent 是拉丁语 per centum，“每一百”。-age 后缀把这个短语变成表示比率的名词，因此 percentage 字面上就是“每一百里有多少份”的计数结果。

senses.title: The share of a whole
senses.definition: a proportion of a total, expressed or understood as a rate out of a hundred
senses.definitionCN: 总量中的一份，以百为基数表示或理解
senses.example: A large percentage of the students live on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 很大比例的学生住在校内。
senses.why: Once the hundred-part strip is drawn, any whole can be mapped onto it. The percentage becomes a way of comparing shares from different totals, which is why it is the standard language of surveys.
senses.whyCN: 一百格长条一旦画好，任何整体都能映射上去。百分比于是成为比较不同总量中份额的方式，因此它成了调查的标准语言。

senses.title: A rate of change
senses.definition: a figure expressing how much something has increased or decreased relative to its earlier level
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物相对先前水平增加或减少多少的数值
senses.example: Sales fell by a small percentage last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度销售额小幅下降。
senses.why: A change can be measured against the old total, and the old total can be treated as one hundred. The percentage then describes the movement rather than the thing moved.
senses.whyCN: 变化可以对照旧总量来量，而旧总量可以被当作一百。于是百分比描述的是“移动了多少”，而不是被移动的那个东西。

senses.title: A percentage point
senses.definition: one unit of difference between two percentages, as opposed to a relative change
senses.definitionCN: 两个百分比之间相差的一个单位，区别于相对变化
senses.example: The rate moved from ten to twelve percent, a rise of two percentage points.
senses.exampleCN: 比率从百分之十升到百分之十二，上升了两个百分点。
senses.why: A change from ten to twelve percent is a fifth in relative terms but only two units on the hundred-grid. English keeps the grid unit separate with the phrase percentage point, precisely to stop the two readings from being confused.
senses.whyCN: 从百分之十到百分之十二，相对变化是五分之一，但在百格图上只移动了两格。英语用 percentage point 单独命名这个格子单位，正是为了不让两种读法混淆。

senses.title: A commission: a percentage of the deal
senses.titleCN: 佣金：交易额的一个百分比
senses.definition: a share of a sale or profit paid to an agent, calculated as a rate per hundred
senses.definitionCN: 按每百比率计算、支付给代理人的销售额或利润份额
senses.example: The agent takes a percentage of every sale.
senses.exampleCN: 代理人从每笔销售中抽取一定比例的佣金。
senses.why: Commerce needed a neutral way to divide a deal without naming a fixed sum. A percentage lets the payment scale with the sale, so the rate itself becomes the agreement.
senses.whyCN: 商业需要一种中立方式来分配交易，而不必写死一个金额。百分比让报酬随销售额缩放，于是“比率”本身就成了协议。

senses.title: A chance, stated per hundred
senses.titleCN: 以百为基数陈述的概率
senses.definition: a probability or likelihood expressed as a rate out of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 以一百为基数表示的可能性或概率
senses.example: There is only a small percentage chance of rain tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很小。
senses.why: Probability is already a number between zero and one. Scaling it to a hundred makes it readable without decimals, and the word carries that scaling rather than the underlying mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 概率本来是零到一之间的数。把它放大到一百，就能不用小数直接读懂，而这个词承载的正是这个缩放，而不是底层的数学。

senses.title: The composition of a mixture
senses.definition: the proportion of a component in a substance, alloy, or mixture
senses.definitionCN: 某一成分在物质、合金或混合物中所占的比例
senses.example: The alloy contains a small percentage of nickel.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金含有少量镍。
senses.why: Recipes and specifications need shares that hold at any batch size. Percentage gives a composition that can be reproduced in a laboratory or a factory without fixing the absolute amounts.
senses.whyCN: 配方与规格需要一种在任何批量下都成立的份额。百分比给出一种可在实验室或工厂复现的成分，而不必固定绝对用量。

senses.title: What is in it for me: no percentage in it
senses.titleCN: 有没有好处：no percentage in it
senses.definition: informally, an advantage or profit to be gained from an action
senses.definitionCN: 口语中，从某项行动中可获得的好处或利益
senses.example: There is no percentage in arguing with him.
senses.exampleCN: 和他争论没有任何好处。
senses.why: If a share can be counted per hundred, it can also be counted for oneself. The slang sense asks what share of the gain comes back to me, and drops the arithmetic while keeping the self-interest.
senses.whyCN: 如果份额可以按百计算，也就可以为自己计算。这一俚语义问的是“收益中有多少回到我这儿”，它丢掉了算术，却保留了私利。

intro.en: Percentage is a modern English noun built on percent, which came from Latin per centum. Its root is centum 'hundred', unrelated to the capere of perceive; only the per- is shared.
intro.cn: percentage 是建立在 percent 之上的现代英语名词，而 percent 来自拉丁语 per centum。其词根是 centum“百”，与 perceive 的 capere 无关；两者只共享 per- 这个前缀。

items.en: Percent and the phrase per cent are recorded, from Italian per cento and Modern Latin per centum, both meaning 'by the hundred'. The expression was used in commercial arithmetic.
items.cn: percent 与短语 per cent 记录于 16 世纪 60 年代，来自意大利语 per cento 与近代拉丁语 per centum，二者都意为“每一百”。这一表达用于商业算术。

items.en: Centum is the Latin word for 'one hundred'. It is generally connected with PIE *dekm- 'ten', through an extended form, though the exact prehistory is source uncertain.
items.cn: centum 是拉丁语“一百”。一般把它通过一个扩展形式连到原始印欧语 *dekm-“十”，但其确切史前过程来源不确定。

items.en: Percentage is formed in English from percent plus the noun suffix -age. It names the rate itself rather than the phrase 'per cent'.
items.cn: percentage 于 1789 年由 percent 加名词后缀 -age 构成。它命名比率本身，而不是 per cent 这个短语。

items.en: The commercial sense 'a commission or allowance calculated as a rate' is recorded. Percentage becomes a standard word in trade and finance.
items.cn: “按比率计算的佣金或酬金”这一商业义记录于 1862 年。percentage 成为贸易与金融中的标准词。

items.en: Statistics and polling make percentage a everyday unit, and percentage point is coined to separate an absolute difference of two rates from a relative change. The slang sense 'advantage' also spreads.
items.cn: 统计学与民调让 percentage 成为日常单位，并造出 percentage point，以区分两个比率的绝对差与相对变化。俚语义“好处”也随之扩散。

note.en: The first group is the percent cluster, where the forms are easy to mix up; the second compares words for shares and rates.
note.cn: 第一组是 percent 词群，几种形式容易混用；第二组比较表示“份额与比率”的词。

entries.definition: the rate itself, as in five percent. It is the number or phrase; percentage is the noun for such a rate in general.
entries.definitionCN: 比率本身，如 five percent。它是数字或短语；percentage 是泛指这类比率的名词。

entries.definition: one unit of absolute difference between two percentages. It prevents a rise from ten to twelve percent being called a two percent rise.
entries.definitionCN: 两个百分比之间绝对差的一个单位。它避免把百分之十到十二说成“上升百分之二”。

entries.definition: a value below which a given percentage of observations fall. It is a position in a distribution, not a share of a total.
entries.definitionCN: 有给定百分比的观测值低于该值。它是分布中的位置，不是整体中的份额。

entries.definition: the British two-word spelling of percent. It is the same phrase, written apart and often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: percent 的英式分写形式。同一个短语，分开写，常用于名词前。

entries.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole. It needs no hundred as a base, while percentage always does.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于整体来考虑的一部分。它不必以百为基数，而 percentage 总是以百为基数。

entries.definition: a part given to or held by someone. It is concrete and often possessive, while percentage is a neutral rate.
entries.definitionCN: 分给或由某人持有的一份。它具体、常含归属，而 percentage 是中性的比率。

entries.definition: a measure of one quantity against another. It is the broader category, and a percentage is one kind of rate.
entries.definitionCN: 一个量对另一个量的度量。它是更宽的类别，percentage 是其中一种比率。

entries.definition: a numerical part of a whole, written as one number over another. It is exact and flexible, while a percentage fixes the denominator at one hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的数值部分，写作一个数比另一个数。它精确而灵活，而 percentage 把分母固定为一百。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on per + cent + age, then three abstract images about the hundred-grid.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 per + cent + age 的挂钩，再用三个关于“百格图”的抽象画面。

normal.en: per cent is Latin for 'by the hundred'. Percentage is that phrase turned into a noun.
normal.cn: per cent 是拉丁语“每一百”。percentage 就是把这个短语变成名词。

normal.en: cent means hundred: a century is a hundred years, a cent is a hundredth of a dollar, a percentage is a rate per hundred.
normal.cn: cent 是“百”：一世纪是一百年，一美分是一美元的百分之一，percentage 是每一百的比率。

normal.en: Draw a strip of one hundred squares. Colour thirty. You have just drawn thirty percentage.
normal.cn: 画一条一百格的长条，涂三十格。你刚刚画出了百分之三十。

normal.en: Percentage point is the grid unit; percent change is the relative jump. Two different rulers for the same move.
normal.cn: 百分点是格子单位；百分比变化是相对跳跃。同一次移动，两把不同的尺。

normal.en: No percentage in it means no slice of the gain comes back to you.
normal.cn: no percentage in it 意思是收益里没有一片回到你手上。

abstract.en: A percentage is a machine for comparing unequal wholes: it maps every total onto the same hundred squares.
abstract.cn: 百分比是一台比较不等总量的机器：它把每个总和都映射到同一百格上。

abstract.en: The hundred-grid hides the base. Ten percent of a small thing and ten percent of a large thing look identical on the strip.
abstract.cn: 百格图隐藏了基数。小东西的百分之十与大东西的百分之十，在长条上长得一模一样。

abstract.en: A percentage can describe a share or demand one; the same number is a description in a report and a bill in a contract.
abstract.cn: 百分比可以描述一份，也可以索取一份；同一个数字，在报告里是描述，在合同里是账单。

examples.en: The percentage of households with internet access passed ninety.
examples.cn: 拥有互联网接入的家庭比例超过了百分之九十。

examples.en: Unemployment fell by half a percentage point, which is not the same as falling by half a percent.
examples.cn: 失业率下降了半个百分点，这与下降百分之半不是一回事。

examples.en: The agent works on a percentage rather than a salary.
examples.cn: 这位代理人按比例抽成，而不是拿固定薪水。

dict_mnemonic.note: per 记成“每一”，cent 记成“百”，-age 记成名词：每一百中的多少，就是百分比。
dict_mnemonic.text: per（每一）+ cent（百）+ -age（名词）→ 每一百中的份额 → 百分比、占比、佣金

root: percent（16 世纪 60 年代，来自近代拉丁 per centum“每一百”）+ -age；centum“百”与原始印欧语 *dekm-“十”同源（一般认为）。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the hundred-based rate, then the share of any whole, the rate of change, the single grid point, the commission, the stated chance, the composition of a mixture, and the slang advantage of a deal.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“以百为基数的比率”开始，转到任何整体中的占比、变化的比率、单个格子即百分点、佣金、被陈述的概率、混合物的成分比例，最后落到口语中一笔交易的好处。

core.en: A strip of one hundred squares with some of them coloured in
core.cn: 一条一百格的长条，其中若干格被涂上颜色

chain: WHAT IS IN IT FOR ME

branches.en: The instrument and its use: a rate per hundred, and any whole mapped onto it.
branches.cn: 工具及其用途：每一百的比率，以及被映射上去的任何整体。

branches.en: Movement on the grid: a relative change, and the single point that separates two rates.
branches.cn: 格子上的移动：相对变化，以及把两个比率分开的单个点。

branches.en: The share that comes back: a commission, and the slang gain for oneself.
branches.cn: 回到手中的份额：佣金，以及俚语里为自己算的那份好处。

branches.en: Probability: a chance written per hundred.
branches.cn: 概率：写成每一百的机会。

branches.en: Composition: the recipe of a mixture, expressed on the same hundred-grid.
branches.cn: 成分：混合物的配方，也表达在同一张百格图上。

intro.en: Percentage belongs to the cent- family, which is large and stable: percent, percentage point, percentile, and the older hundred words cent, century, centennial.
intro.cn: percentage 属于 cent- 词族，这个族大而稳定：percent、percentage point、percentile，以及更古老的“百”词 cent、century、centennial。

latinIntro.en: Latin centum 'hundred' gives the stem, and the phrase per centum 'by the hundred' gives percent. The suffix -age is native French-derived English, so the word mixes a Latin base with a Romance noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum“百”提供词干，短语 per centum“每一百”给出 percent。后缀 -age 是经法语进入英语的，因此这个词把拉丁词基与罗曼语名词词尾混合在一起。

items.meaning: in each hundred; a hundred-based rate
items.meaningCN: 每一百中；以百为基数的比率

items.meaning: a rate or share expressed per hundred
items.meaningCN: 以百表示的比率或份额

items.meaning: one unit of difference between two percentages
items.meaningCN: 两个百分比之间相差的一个单位
items.example: The gap narrowed by one percentage point.
items.exampleCN: 差距缩小了一个百分点。

items.meaning: the value below which a given percentage falls
items.meaningCN: 有给定百分比低于其下的值；百分位数
items.example: She scored in the ninetieth percentile.
items.exampleCN: 她的成绩位于第九十百分位。

items.meaning: the same phrase, written as two words
items.meaningCN: 同一个短语，分写为两个词
items.example: A five per cent rise was announced.
items.exampleCN: 宣布了百分之五的涨幅。

items.meaningCN: 一美元的百分之一；美分

items.meaning: a period of one hundred years
items.example: The bridge stood for a century.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥矗立了一个世纪。

items.example: The town held a centennial parade.
items.exampleCN: 小镇举行了一百周年游行。

items.meaning: a temperature scale of one hundred steps
items.meaningCN: 分为一百度的温标；摄氏
items.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees centigrade.

latinEntries.example: Centum is the base of percent and century.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 是 percent 与 century 的词基。

latinEntries.meaning: by the hundred; for each hundred
latinEntries.exampleCN: per centum 变成英语 percent。

latinEntries.meaning: a division of a hundred men; a hundred
latinEntries.example: Centuria is the source of English century.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centuria 是英语 century 的来源。

definition_zh: 知觉；感知；看法；观念；洞察力；感知能力；印象；公众认知；机器感知
definition_en: the act or result of becoming aware of something through the senses or the mind, the view a person or public holds, keen insight, or the process by which a system interprets input
core_image: 眼睛和耳朵把外面的世界收进一张内部地图，再给上面的每样东西写上名字
scene: 同一场雨，有人只听见噪音，有人听出雨势在变小。Two people hear the same rain differently, and the difference lies in perception.
sceneCN: 这里 perception 是「感知能力」（第 4 个义项：感官对细微差别作出分辨的能力）；句意：两个人听同一场雨听到的不一样，差别就在感知能力；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 知觉；感知；看法；观念；洞察力；印象

derivatives.zh: 有洞察力的；感知敏锐的

senses.title: Awareness through the senses
senses.definition: the act or result of becoming aware of objects and events through sight, hearing, touch, taste, or smell
senses.definitionCN: 通过视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉或嗅觉觉察物体与事件的行为或结果
senses.example: Perception of the low hum came before any conscious thought.
senses.exampleCN: 对那阵低鸣的知觉出现在任何有意识的想法之前。
senses.why: Percipere is per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'to take': the senses take the world in and hold it. Perception is that grasping, the moment the outer world becomes an inner object.
senses.whyCN: percipere 是 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取”：感官把世界拿进来并握住。perception 就是这一抓，是外部世界变成内部对象的那一刻。

senses.title: The grasp the mind forms
senses.definition: the mental understanding or interpretation a person forms about a situation, often beyond bare sensory data
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某种情况形成的理解或解释，常超出纯粹的感官材料
senses.example: Her perception of the risk was sharper than the numbers suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 她对风险的判断比数字显示的更敏锐。
senses.why: The hand that takes can also sort and name. Once the inner map is drawn, perception means not only seeing the shape but understanding what it is.
senses.whyCN: 拿取的那只手也会分类和命名。内部地图画好之后，perception 不仅指看见形状，还指明白它是什么。

senses.title: The view people hold
senses.definition: the opinion, image, or belief that a person or the public holds about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或公众对某人某事持有的看法、形象或信念
senses.example: Public perception of the agency improved after the open day.
senses.exampleCN: 开放日之后，公众对该机构的看法有所改善。
senses.why: Many inner maps can agree. When they do, perception becomes a social fact: not what is out there, but what a group has taken in and agreed to see.
senses.whyCN: 许多内部地图可以彼此一致。一旦一致，perception 就成了社会事实：不是外面有什么，而是一个群体拿进来并同意看见什么。

senses.title: Keenness of sensing
senses.definition: the acuity or fineness of a person's or animal's senses in detecting small differences
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的感官在察觉细微差别时的敏锐程度
senses.example: A dog's perception of scent far exceeds a human's.
senses.exampleCN: 狗对气味的感知能力远远超过人。
senses.why: The same hand can be strong or weak. This sense speaks of the instrument rather than the object: a fine net takes more of the sea than a coarse one.
senses.whyCN: 同一只手可以有力或无力。这个义项说的是工具本身而不是对象：细网比粗网能从海里捞起更多东西。

senses.title: Insight into what is hidden
senses.definition: the ability to notice and understand things that are not obvious to others, especially motives or patterns
senses.definitionCN: 察觉并理解他人不易看到之事的能力，尤指动机或规律
senses.example: With unusual perception, she named the fear behind his joke.
senses.exampleCN: 她以不寻常的洞察力，说出了他玩笑背后的恐惧。
senses.why: Perception can go through the surface to the structure beneath it. The eye does not just receive; it reads the map for what the map is hiding.
senses.whyCN: 感知可以穿过表层看到下面的结构。眼睛不只是接收，它还读地图，读出地图藏起来的东西。

senses.title: The field that studies sensing
senses.definition: the branch of psychology and neuroscience that studies how organisms organize and interpret sensory information
senses.definitionCN: 心理学与神经科学中研究生物如何组织并解释感官信息的分支
senses.example: The paper reviews fifty years of research on visual perception.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文回顾了视觉知觉五十年的研究。
senses.why: When the act becomes a subject, perception turns into a field with methods and experiments. The word no longer names one grasping but the laws of grasping in general.
senses.whyCN: 当这个行为成为研究对象时，perception 变成一门有方法与实验的学科。这个词不再命名某一次抓取，而是抓取的一般规律。

senses.title: What is sensed versus what is real
senses.titleCN: 所感与所实之间的距离
senses.definition: in philosophy, the relation between sensory appearance and the object or reality that is believed to cause it
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中感官显现与被认为是其成因的对象或实在之间的关系
senses.example: The argument turns on whether perception gives us the object itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这一论证的关键在于：知觉是否把对象本身给了我们。
senses.why: The inner map may not match the land. Philosophy uses perception for the whole problem of whether the copy in the mind is faithful to what lies outside it.
senses.whyCN: 内部地图未必与真实地形相符。哲学用 perception 指整个问题：心里的副本是否忠实地对应外面的东西。

senses.title: The impression others receive
senses.definition: the impression a person or organization creates in others, especially through appearance, tone, and manner
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或组织在他人心中造成的印象，尤指通过外表、语气与举止
senses.example: His calm voice shaped the jury's perception of him as honest.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的声音让陪审团觉得他是个诚实的人。
senses.why: Here the map is drawn in another person's head. Perception is the image you did not write but caused, and it can diverge sharply from what you intended.
senses.whyCN: 这里的地图画在别人的头脑里。perception 是你没有亲手写、却由你造成的形象，它可以与你原本的意图相差很远。

senses.title: A machine interpreting input
senses.definition: the process by which a computer system detects, classifies, and interprets signals from cameras, microphones, or other sensors
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统检测、分类并解释来自摄像头、麦克风或其他传感器的信号的过程
senses.example: Machine perception lets the car read the road markings.
senses.exampleCN: 机器感知让汽车能读懂路面标线。
senses.why: Engineers build the same loop with silicon: a sensor takes in, a model names. The word keeps its shape even when the eye is a camera and the mind is an algorithm.
senses.whyCN: 工程师用硅片搭出同样的回路：传感器拿进来，模型来命名。即使眼睛变成摄像头、头脑变成算法，这个词的形状也没有变。

intro.en: Perception comes from Latin perceptio, an action noun from percipere 'to take in, grasp, perceive'. Percipere is per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'to take, seize'. English borrowed perception in the 14th century first for the taking in of knowledge or the receiving of impressions, and the modern sensory sense settled in the 19th century with the rise of experimental psychology.
intro.cn: perception 来自拉丁语 perceptio，是 percipere“拿进来、把握、感知”的动作名词。percipere 由 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取、抓取”构成。英语在 14 世纪借入 perception，最初指“接受知识或接收印象”，现代感官义则在 19 世纪随着实验心理学兴起而定型。

items.en: Capere means 'to take, seize, capture'. With per- 'through, thoroughly', percipere means 'to take hold of completely', and by extension 'to grasp with the mind'.
items.cn: capere 意为“拿取、抓取、俘获”。加上 per-“穿过、彻底”，percipere 意为“完全抓住”，引申为“用头脑把握”。

items.en: Perceptio in Latin covers receiving, collecting, and comprehension. The word already lives on the border between the senses and the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 perceptio 同时涵盖接收、收集与理解。这个词从一开始就住在感官与心智的边界上。

items.en: English perception first means the receiving of impressions or the act of understanding, especially in religious and legal prose.
items.cn: 英语 perception 最早指接收印象或理解的行为，尤见于宗教与法律文字。

items.en: Philosophy makes perception a central term in the debate over what the mind directly knows: ideas, impressions, or external objects.
items.cn: 哲学使 perception 成为争论的核心术语，争论的问题是心智直接知道什么：观念、印象，还是外部对象。

items.en: Experimental psychology separates sensation from perception: sensation is raw input, perception is the organized interpretation of it.
items.cn: 实验心理学把感觉与知觉分开：感觉是原始输入，知觉是对它的有组织解释。

items.en: The word extends to social perception in politics and to machine perception in computing, keeping the same loop of taking in and naming.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到政治中的社会认知与计算中的机器感知，保留着同一个“拿进来再命名”的回路。

note.en: The first group separates the percept family from two words that look close but have different roots. The second group compares sensation, cognition, view, and insight, the four words most often put in perception's place.
note.cn: 第一组把 percept 词族与两个形近但词根不同的词分开。第二组比较感觉、认知、看法与洞察力，这四个词最常被用来替代 perception。

entries.definition: the object or content of a perception, the thing as sensed rather than as thought. Perception names the act, percept names what is taken in.
entries.definitionCN: 知觉的对象或内容，即被感觉到而非被思考的东西。perception 命名行为，percept 命名被拿进来的东西。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It describes a person's ability, while perception can name the act, the view, or the field of study.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉与理解的。它描述人的能力，而 perception 可以命名行为、看法或学科。

entries.definition: a point of view or the art of drawing depth. Its root is specere 'to look', not capere 'to take', so it names where you look from, not what you take in.
entries.definitionCN: 观点，或描绘深度的技法。它的词根是 specere“看”，不是 capere“拿取”，所以它命名的是你从哪里看，而不是你拿进了什么。

entries.definition: a rate per hundred. Its per- is the same, but the root is centum 'hundred', so it has nothing to do with taking or sensing.
entries.definitionCN: 以百为基数的比率。它的 per- 相同，但词根是 centum“一百”，与拿取或感知毫无关系。

entries.definition: a feeling or impression produced by stimulation of a sense organ. It is the raw input that perception organizes and interprets.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉器官受刺激产生的感受或印象。它是知觉加以组织与解释的原始输入。

entries.definition: the mental processes of knowing, remembering, and reasoning. It is the wider mental side, of which perception is the entry stage.
entries.definitionCN: 知道、记忆与推理的心理过程。它是更宽的心智面，而知觉是其中的入口阶段。

entries.definition: an opinion held and usually expressed. It is the social sense of perception made explicit and arguable.
entries.definitionCN: 持有并通常会表达的意见。它是 perception 社会义的外显、可争论版本。

entries.definition: a deep and accurate understanding of something hidden or complex. It is the sharpest end of perception, where the map reveals its own structure.
entries.definitionCN: 对隐藏或复杂事物的深刻而准确的理解。它是感知最锐利的一端，此时地图显露出自身的结构。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: per- 'thoroughly', capere 'take', perceptio, the sensation/perception split in 19th-century psychology, and the specere/centum traps.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：per-“彻底”、capere“拿取”、perceptio、19 世纪心理学对感觉与知觉的划分，以及 specere 与 centum 两个陷阱。

normal.en: Per- is 'thoroughly' and capere is 'take': perception is the senses taking the world in completely enough to hold it.
normal.cn: per- 是“彻底”，capere 是“拿取”：perception 就是感官把世界拿进来，拿得足够完整以便握住。

normal.en: Cavere and capture share the same capere family; perception is capture without a fight, the world seized by the eye.
normal.cn: cavere 与 capture 同属 capere 词族；perception 是一场没有搏斗的俘获，世界被眼睛抓走。

normal.en: The percept is what is taken in; the perception is the taking; perceptive is the person who takes quickly.
normal.cn: percept 是被拿进来的东西；perception 是拿的行为；perceptive 是拿得快的人。

normal.en: Perspective looks from a place, perception takes something in: the first is about the eye's position, the second about the mind's grasp.
normal.cn: perspective 从某处看出去，perception 把东西拿进来：前者关于眼睛的位置，后者关于头脑的把握。

normal.en: Percentage shares the per- but not the root: centum is 'hundred', so a percentage is a count, not a grasp.
normal.cn: percentage 共享 per- 却不共享词根：centum 是“一百”，所以百分比是计数，不是把握。

abstract.en: The eye is a net; the world is a sea. What you call reality is the catch you happened to bring up.
abstract.cn: 眼睛是一张网，世界是一片海。你称为现实的东西，只是你碰巧捞上来的那一网。

abstract.en: Two people stand in the same rain; one hears noise, one hears the storm weakening. The rain did not change.
abstract.cn: 两个人站在同一场雨里；一个听见噪音，一个听见暴风雨在减弱。雨并没有变。

abstract.en: A public image is a map drawn by strangers, and you cannot revise it with a pen you do not hold.
abstract.cn: 公众形象是陌生人画的地图，你手里没有那支笔，就改不动它。

examples.en: Depth perception depends on having two eyes that work together.
examples.cn: 深度知觉依赖于两只眼睛协同工作。

examples.en: The campaign tried to change public perception of the tax.
examples.cn: 这场宣传活动试图改变公众对这项税收的看法。

examples.en: Her perception of the room's mood was immediate and accurate.
examples.cn: 她对房间气氛的感知既迅速又准确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破塞普申」——眼睛像一只手“破”开外面的世界，把看到的东西“塞”进脑子里 → perception 知觉；看法；洞察力（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 percipere「拿进来、把握、感知」，由 per-「彻底」+ capere「拿取」构成，动作名词为 perceptio。核心是「感官把外面的世界彻底拿进来，在内里画成一张地图」。同族含 perceive、percept、perceptive、perceptual、perceptible；perspective（specere「看」）与 percentage（centum「一百」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of perception all describe a hand taking the world in and drawing a map inside. What changes is what is taken (sensory data, meaning, public opinion), how sharp the hand is, or whether we are naming the act, the field, or the machine that now does the taking.
sensesIntro.cn: perception 的九个义项都描述一只手把世界拿进来、在内里画成地图。变化的是拿进来的东西（感官材料、意义、公众意见）、这只手有多敏锐，以及我们命名的是行为、学科，还是如今承担这件事的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes and ears take the outer world in and draw an inner map with names written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛和耳朵把外面的世界收进一张内部地图，并在上面写下名字。

branches.en: TAKING IN: sensory awareness and the acuity of the instrument that does the taking.
branches.cn: 拿进来：感官觉察，以及执行拿取的那件仪器的敏锐度。

branches.en: READING THE MAP: mental understanding of a situation, and insight into what the map hides.
branches.cn: 读地图：对情境的心智理解，以及看穿地图所藏之物的洞察力。

branches.en: SHARED MAPS: the view a public holds, and the impression one person creates in another's head.
branches.cn: 共享的地图：公众持有的看法，以及一个人在他人头脑中造成的印象。

branches.en: THE STUDY OF THE MAP: experimental psychology of perception, and the philosophical question of whether the map matches the land.
branches.cn: 对地图的研究：实验心理学中的知觉研究，以及地图是否与真实地形相符的哲学问题。

branches.en: THE SILICON EYE: a machine takes in signals and names what it finds.
branches.cn: 硅做的眼睛：机器接收信号并命名它所发现的东西。

intro.en: Perception is percept- plus -ion (Latin -ionem). Percept- comes from Latin percipere, per- 'thoroughly' + capere 'take'. The family splits neatly: -ion the act, -ive the person, -ual the property, -ible the possibility, and percept the object.
intro.cn: perception 是 percept- 加 -ion（拉丁 -ionem）。percept- 出自拉丁 percipere，即 per-“彻底”+ capere“拿取”。词族分工整齐：-ion 行为、-ive 人、-ual 属性、-ible 可能性，percept 则是对象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is capere 'take', percipere 'take in thoroughly', perceptio 'a taking in', and perceptum 'the thing taken in'. The same capere with other prefixes gives receive, accept, intercept, and participate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 capere“拿取”、percipere“彻底拿进来”、perceptio“拿进来这件事”、perceptum“被拿进来之物”。同一个 capere 配上其他前缀，还产生表示“接收”“接受”“拦截”与“参与”的词。

items.meaning: the act or result of taking in through the senses or mind
items.meaningCN: 通过感官或心智拿进来的行为或结果（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Perception of the signal dropped in the fog.
items.exampleCN: 雾中对该信号的感知减弱了。

items.meaning: to become aware of, to take in
items.meaningCN: 察觉；把……收入感知（per- 彻底 + capere 拿取）
items.example: They perceived a change in his tone.
items.exampleCN: 他们察觉到他的语气变了。

items.structure: Latin perceptum, neuter past participle of percipere
items.meaning: the object or content of a perception
items.example: The percept is the red patch, not the apple itself.
items.exampleCN: 知觉对象是那块红色，而不是苹果本身。

items.meaningCN: 察觉与理解敏捷的；有洞察力的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: A perceptive reader notices the repeated image.
items.exampleCN: 有洞察力的读者会注意到反复出现的意象。

items.meaning: relating to perception as a process
items.meaningCN: 与知觉过程有关的（-ual 形容词）
items.exampleCN: 知觉学习会随练习而提高。

items.example: There was a perceptible drop in temperature.

items.meaningCN: 太轻微而察觉不到的（im- 否定）
items.example: The change was imperceptible at first.
items.exampleCN: 起初这一变化察觉不到。

items.meaningCN: 错误的知觉或印象（mis- 错误）
items.exampleCN: 这个错误印象持续了好多年。

items.meaning: a point of view; the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 观点；透视法（per- + specere 看 + -ive）

latinEntries.meaning: that which has been taken in

definition_zh: 完美的；理想的；完全的；使完善；完成时
definition_en: having no fault and being as good as possible; exactly suitable; complete in every way; to make something fully developed
core_image: 一块被反复打磨的木头，棱角全部消失，表面能照出人的影子
scene: 木工房里，老师傅换掉最后一道砂纸，用指腹顺着木纹摸了一遍。He kept sanding until the surface felt perfect under his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 perfect 是「完美的、无可挑剔的」（第 1 个义项：质地没有任何缺陷）；句意是他不肯停手，直到指腹摸到的表面毫无瑕疵。

derivatives.zh: 由 perfect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「完美；完善」
由 perfect 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「完美地；完全地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 perfect 构成，义为「不完美的」
由 perfection 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「完美主义者」

senses.title: Flawless in quality
senses.definition: so good in every detail that no fault can be found
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都好到挑不出毛病
senses.example: Her piano playing is almost perfect.
senses.exampleCN: 她的钢琴演奏几乎无可挑剔。
senses.why: Perfectus is the past participle of a verb meaning to finish thoroughly, so the adjective first says finished, then finished so well that nothing at all is missing.
senses.whyCN: perfectus 本是一个意为「彻底做完」的动词的过去分词，所以这个形容词先说「做完了」，再说「做完到一点都不缺」，于是成了无可挑剔。

senses.title: Exactly suitable
senses.definition: the best possible thing for a particular purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某个用途或某个人来说最合适的那一个
senses.example: The little courtyard is perfect for summer evenings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小院子最适合夏夜。
senses.why: Once a thing is complete, it meets its purpose with nothing left over and nothing short, so the word slides from nothing lacking to nothing mismatched.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦完整，就恰好满足它的用途，既不多余也不欠缺，于是词义从「什么都不缺」滑到「什么都不错配」。

senses.title: Complete, used for emphasis
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean complete, often when someone is surprised or annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前表示「完全的」，常带惊讶或恼火的语气
senses.example: I felt like a perfect fool.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得自己十足是个傻瓜。
senses.why: The old sense of thoroughly done survives here as bare emphasis: nothing is added to the noun except the claim that it is complete all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 「彻底做完」这个旧义在这里变成纯粹的强调：名词之外没有增加任何内容，只多了一句「从头到尾都够彻底」。

senses.title: To make something fully developed
senses.definition: to improve something through repeated work until it reaches its best possible form
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复打磨把某物改进到它能达到的最好状态
senses.example: She perfected her accent by listening to recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠听录音把自己的口音打磨得很地道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin prefix per-, meaning through, and so exposes the work hidden inside the adjective: carrying a thing through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语前缀 per-（穿过、彻底），因此把形容词里藏着的过程露了出来：把一件事一直做到头。

senses.title: The tense of completed action
senses.definition: the verb form that presents an action as finished rather than still going on
senses.definitionCN: 把动作呈现为已经完成、而不是仍在进行的动词形式
senses.example: In the perfect tense, the sentence uses have plus a past participle.
senses.exampleCN: 在完成时里，句子用 have 加过去分词。
senses.why: Grammarians took perfectus in its literal sense of finished and applied it to a verb form whose whole job is to say that an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家取 perfectus 字面上的「已完成」，把它安在一种专门表示动作已经做完的动词形式上。

intro.en: Perfect is built from two Latin pieces, a prefix meaning through and a verb meaning to make, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: perfect 由两个拉丁成分拼成，一个意为「彻底」的前缀，一个意为「做」的动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The verb perficere joined per-, through, to facere, to do or make: to carry something through to the end.
items.cn: 动词 perficere 由表「穿过、彻底」的 per- 与 facere（做、造）组合，意为把一件事做到底。

items.en: Its past participle perfectus meant thoroughly made or finished, and only later gathered the sense of excellent quality.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 perfectus 意为「彻底做成的、完成的」，后来才带上称赞质量的意思。
